tools_helpful.evidence: Bootstrap ran successfully, created MIGRATION-MAPPING.md with 7 rows, injected inline TODOs, set up project scaffold — enabled structured migration workflow.
Validator reported all PASS (residue grep, TODO markers, mapping integrity, manifest, build). Caught WARN for MIGRATION-DEFERRED.md consistency and smoke launch environment issue.
Agent used anchored pattern lookups to resolve TODO markers without loading the full MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md.

failed_apis.why_tried: UWP source uses Windows.UI.Colors.RoyalBlue, Windows.UI.Colors.LightGray etc. inline in code-behind for input event handlers and manipulation color feedback.
failed_apis.root_cause: Bootstrap rewrites 'using' statements but does not rewrite inline fully-qualified references like 'Windows.UI.Colors.RoyalBlue'. The namespace mapping table in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md covers the mapping but doesn't warn about inline qualified references surviving the bootstrap.
failed_apis.fix: Agent replaced all Windows.UI.Colors with Microsoft.UI.Colors across multiple files in a single PowerShell batch.

failed_apis.why_tried: UWP PointerPoint has a .PointerDevice property (returns PointerDevice object) used to check PointerDeviceType. In WinUI 3, this property was removed — PointerDeviceType is accessed directly on PointerPoint.
failed_apis.root_cause: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md has no entry for this API change. The bootstrap didn't inject a TODO for it.

special_apis.special_handling: In WinUI 3, PointerDeviceType is a direct property on PointerPoint, not accessed via the intermediate PointerDevice object as in UWP.

errors_encountered.error: CS0234: The type or namespace name 'Colors' does not exist in the namespace 'Windows.UI'
errors_encountered.root_cause: Bootstrap rewrites using statements but inline fully-qualified references like Windows.UI.Colors.RoyalBlue survive. Multiple files (1-InputEvents.xaml.cs, 4-XAMLManipulations.xaml.cs, 5-GestureRecognizer.xaml.cs) had these references.
errors_encountered.fix: Batch PowerShell replace of Windows.UI.Colors with Microsoft.UI.Colors across all affected files.

errors_encountered.error: CS1061: 'PointerPoint' does not contain a definition for 'PointerDevice'
errors_encountered.root_cause: WinUI 3 removed PointerPoint.PointerDevice property; PointerDeviceType is now directly on PointerPoint. No skill guidance covers this change.

dev_agent_struggles.where: Build cycle after migrating all files (lines 992-1115 in build-events.jsonl)
dev_agent_struggles.symptom: First build failed with ~30 CS0234 errors (Windows.UI.Colors) and 2 CS1061 errors (PointerPoint.PointerDevice) across multiple files.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: 2 failed builds (lines 992, 994), then 1 successful build (line 1115). Agent fixed both issues in a single fix cycle (~60 event lines).
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Bootstrap namespace rewrite only handles 'using' statements, not inline fully-qualified type references. PointerPoint API change not documented.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Agent correctly identified both issues from error messages, batch-replaced Colors namespace and manually fixed PointerDevice property access.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: 1) Bootstrap script should also rewrite inline fully-qualified namespace references (Windows.UI.Colors.X → Microsoft.UI.Colors.X). 2) Add PointerPoint.PointerDevice → PointerPoint.PointerDeviceType to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md adaptable API list.

env_issues.issue: Smoke launch reported WARN — could not launch the app (environment/deploy issue, not a code defect)
env_issues.workaround: Validator correctly classified this as non-fatal WARN rather than FAIL. The app was verified to build and run successfully via separate dotnet run.
